title: Normalized Tor of a regular quotient with annihilated coefficients
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ be a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] with $r\geq0$, put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and $B=A/I$, and let $M$ be any $B$-module. Tor is computed by augmented projective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. The classes $\bar f_j$ form a $B$-basis of $I/I^2$. There are canonical $B$-linear isomorphisms, natural in $M$,
$$c_{A,I,M,q}:\bigwedge_B^q(I/I^2)\otimes_B M\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tor}_q^A(B,M)\quad(q\geq0).$$
For every regular generating tuple of $I$, its Koszul resolution [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] computes $c_{A,I,M,q}$ by sending $(\bar f_{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_{j_q})\otimes m$ to the homology class of $(e_{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{j_q})\otimes m$. This prescription is independent of the regular generating tuple and of augmentation-preserving resolution comparison maps. For a flat ring homomorphism $A\to A'$, put $I'=IA'$, $B'=A'/I'$ and $M'=B'\otimes_BM$. If $B'=0$, define $c_{A',I',M',q}$ to be the unique map between zero modules; otherwise the image tuple is again regular. Under the canonical flat-base-change maps for conormal modules and Tor, $B'\otimes_Bc_{A,I,M,q}$ equals $c_{A',I',M',q}$. These compatibilities respect identities and composition. The assertion includes $r=0$; for $I=A$ separately extend the prescription by the unique zero-module maps (all $B$-modules then vanish); both sides vanish for $q>r$.

proof.text: Apply the conormal-basis theorem to $f$: write $N=I/I^2$ and $b_j=\bar f_j$, a $B$-basis. Regularity implies Koszul regularity, so the normalized-resolution theorem supplies $K=K_A(f)$ as a projective resolution of $B$, with augmentation $K_0=A\to B$ the quotient map. Thus the resolution comparison $\iota_{K,M}$ identifies $\operatorname{Tor}^A_q(B,M)$ with $H_q(K\otimes_A M)$. All three inputs allow the empty tuple; the original regularity hypothesis makes $B\ne0$.

source.place: Tags 062F (lemma-regular-koszul-regular) and 062I (lemma-H1-regular-quasi-regular), first paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 00LY and 00LN

proof.text: Every coefficient of the Koszul differential is an $f_j$, so $d\otimes1_M=0$ because $IM=0$. Consequently $H_q(K\otimes_A M)=K_q\otimes_A M$. The exterior-basis theorem gives the increasing wedges $e_J$ as an $A$-basis of $K_q$ and $b_J$ as a $B$-basis of $\bigwedge_B^qN$. Both $K_q\otimes_A M$ and $(\bigwedge_B^qN)\otimes_B M$ are therefore direct sums of copies of $M$ indexed by the same increasing subsets $J$: the mutually inverse maps send $b_J\otimes m$ to $e_J\otimes m$ and back. Compose this isomorphism with $\iota_{K,M}^{-1}$ to define $c^f_{M,q}$. This proves exactly the displayed normalization, without requiring $M$ flat.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), explicit differential following Tag 0622; algebra.tex Tag 00DM, increasing-wedge basis

proof.text: For a $B$-linear map $u:M\to L$, both coefficient maps send $b_J\otimes m$ to the class of $e_J\otimes u(m)$. The second-variable clause of the resolution-lift theorem identifies the latter with $\operatorname{Tor}^A_q(B,u)$, proving naturality. The $B$-action on Tor is the action from its coefficient module: scalar multiplication by $b\in B$ is the map induced by $m\mapsto bm$. On $K\otimes_A M$ it is $e_J\otimes m\mapsto e_J\otimes bm$. The displayed construction is therefore $B$-linear. This action restricts to the original $A$-action and is independent of the resolution by the same comparison formula.

source.place: Tags 00LZ (lemma-tor-welldefined) and 00LY (section-tor), functoriality in the second variable

proof.text: Let $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ be any other regular generating tuple for $I$. Choose $a_{ij}\in A$ with $g_j=\sum_i a_{ij}f_i$ and put $t:A^s\to A^r$, $t(e'_j)=\sum_i a_{ij}e_i$. Applying $t$ to every factor of a wedge is well defined: the tensor-algebra map preserves the relations $v\otimes v=0$. It gives $U_q=\bigwedge^q t$. If $\varphi_f(e_i)=f_i$ and $\varphi_g(e'_j)=g_j$, then $\varphi_f t=\varphi_g$; the differential formula gives, on a pure wedge, $d_fU(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_q)=\sum_k(-1)^{k+1}\varphi_g(v_k)t(v_1)\wedge\cdots\widehat{t(v_k)}\cdots\wedge t(v_q)=Ud_g(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_q)$. Thus $U:K_A(g)\to K_A(f)$ is a chain map with $U_0=1_A$, preserving the quotient augmentations. Neither a square matrix nor an invertible matrix over $A$ was used.

source.place: Tags 0622 and 0623, differential formula; algebra.tex Tag 00DM, tensor-quotient construction of exterior algebra

proof.text: Modulo $I$, the same matrix satisfies $\bar g_j=\sum_i\bar a_{ij}\bar f_i$ in $N$. Tensoring the preceding map with $M$ consequently carries $e'_{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e'_{j_q}\otimes m$ to the expansion, in the $f$ wedge coordinates, of $(\bar g_{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar g_{j_q})\otimes m$. Both Koszul complexes are the normalized resolutions supplied in step 1 for their respective regular tuples. The first-variable resolution-lift theorem, applied to $1_B$ and $U$, says $\iota_{K(f),M}=H_q(U\otimes1_M)\iota_{K(g),M}$. Comparing the preceding values proves $c^g_{M,q}=c^f_{M,q}$ on all generators, hence everywhere. The same theorem says any augmentation-preserving lift computes that identical map on Tor, so choices of $a_{ij}$, comparison maps, and projective resolutions do not affect $c$.

source.place: Tag 00LZ (lemma-tor-welldefined), identity and independence-of-lift clauses; agent-supplied coefficient generator comparison

proof.text: Let $A\to A'$ be flat. For each prefix ideal $J_j=(f_1,\ldots,f_j)$, quotient tensor identifies $A'\otimes_A A/J_j$ with $A'/J_jA'$. Flat tensor exactness preserves the injective multiplication maps by $f_j$ on $A/J_{j-1}$. The image tuple is therefore weakly regular and, if $B'\ne0$, regular in the stated convention. Flat tensor exactness applied to $0\to I\to A\to B\to0$ identifies $A'\otimes_A I$ with $I'$. Apply it also to $0\to I^2\to I\to N\to0$. Since $(I')^2=I^2A'$ (expand products of finite sums of elements of $IA'$), its cokernel gives the conormal isomorphism $B'\otimes_B N\cong I'/(I')^2$, $b'\otimes\bar x\mapsto b'\overline{x'}$. The replacement of $A'\otimes_A N$ by $B'\otimes_B N$ uses $IN=0$ and the tensor-over-quotient isomorphism. This sends every $1\otimes\bar f_j$ to $\overline{f'_j}$.

Assume $B'\ne0$. Scalar extension identifies $A'\otimes_A K_A(f)$ with $K_{A'}(f')$: on degree $q$ it sends $a'\otimes e_J$ to $a'e'_J$, an isomorphism by the exterior bases; the differential formula and quotient augmentations agree on these elements. Flat tensor exactness makes this a resolution of $B'$. Put $C_q=K_q\otimes_A M$ and reindex $C_q$ as the bounded cochain complex $C^{-q}$ supported in $[-r,0]$. Flat cohomology base change gives $A'\otimes_A H_q(C)\cong H_q(A'\otimes_A C)$. Identify $A'\otimes_A M$ with $M'=B'\otimes_BM$ by tensor over the quotient. Associativity here sends $a'\otimes(x\otimes m)$ to $(a'\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes m)$, with inverse multiplying the two $A'$ scalars. With the normalized Tor identifications this is the canonical flat-base-change map $B'\otimes_B\operatorname{Tor}^A_q(B,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tor}^{A'}_q(B',M')$; the replacement by a tensor over $B$ uses the action in step 3. Its cycle formula is $b'\otimes[z]\mapsto[b'\otimes z]$. Resolution-lift naturality makes it independent of the selected comparison maps.

source.place: Tag 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), proof: flat tensor commutes with cohomology; more-algebra.tex Tag 062H, displayed Koszul scalar extension in its proof; algebra.tex Tag 00LZ

proof.text: The exterior base-change map is $b'\otimes(n_1\wedge\cdots\wedge n_q)\mapsto b'(n'_1\wedge\cdots\wedge n'_q)$, where $n'_j=1\otimes n_j$. In the conormal bases of step 6 it identifies the increasing-wedge bases, so is an isomorphism. On $b'\otimes(b_J\otimes m)$ both paths of the desired square now give the Tor class of $e'_J\otimes(b'\otimes m)$, by steps 2 and 7. These tensors generate, proving equality of the maps. For two successive flat maps $A\to A'\to A''$, the tensor associativity identification sends $b''\otimes(b'\otimes z)$ to $b''b'\otimes z$ (with the image of $b'$ understood). Both the conormal map and the Tor cycle map obey this formula; their composites therefore equal the direct maps. For the identity ring map they send $1\otimes z$ to $z$. The coefficient naturality square has the same verification with $m$ replaced by $u(m)$. Thus the compatibilities respect identities and composition.

source.place: Tags 00DM and 00CV: exterior and tensor generators; agent-supplied explicit compatibility squares

proof.text: If $r=0$, then $I=0$, $N=0$, and $K$ has only $K_0=A$; the construction is $B\otimes_BM=M\cong\operatorname{Tor}^A_0(A,M)$ in degree zero and the unique zero maps in positive degrees. For any $r$, the exterior-basis theorem gives zero terms on both sides for $q>r$. If $B'=0$, every $B'$-module, including $M'$ and both sides after base change, is zero; the same compatibility squares are equalities of unique maps. The separately stipulated case $I=A$ likewise has $M=0$ and all tensor and Tor complexes zero; no nonexistent regular tuple for the unit ideal is asserted. This also covers $A=0$. An intermediate zero quotient stays zero under further scalar extension, so the composition assertion covers these cases too.
